title: Virtual Color Mixer
description: Three knobs send red, green and blue values to your computer to mix a colour.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 3 × knob (10 kΩ potentiometer), and some jumper wires.
Push the knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. One outer leg of the knob → that same row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the knob to GND.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's 5V pin → the red + row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The knob's other outer leg → that same row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the knob's middle leg to pin A0 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A0 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the knob's middle leg to pin A0.

steps.clip: Push a second knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the second knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one outer leg of the second knob to the blue − row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the second knob to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second knob's other outer leg to the red + row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the second knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the second knob's middle leg to pin A1 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A1 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the second knob's middle leg to pin A1.

steps.clip: Push a third knob into the breadboard, each of its three legs in its own column.
hints: The two outer legs are for power; the middle leg gives the reading.
steps.goal: Put the third knob on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one outer leg of the third knob to the blue − row.
steps.goal: Connect one outer leg of the third knob to GND.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the third knob's other outer leg to the red + row.
hints: Now the knob has 0 V at one end and 5 V at the other.
steps.goal: Connect the third knob's other outer leg to 5V.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the third knob's middle leg to pin A2 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin A2 is on the ANALOG IN side of the Arduino.
The middle leg's voltage follows the knob: 0 V to 5 V.
steps.goal: Connect the third knob's middle leg to pin A2.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. The Serial Monitor shows three numbers, one per knob. (The official example then mixes them into a colour on your computer with Processing.)
